meaning: The README claims M1 and M5 share a line-for-line identical compliance cascade, that α_v defaults to 0.3, and that it is pinned at 0.3 in all four M5 fits on disk. It is a prose claim about defaults and past fit configuration, not executable code.

could_move.what: If α_v is in fact freed rather than pinned, fitted compliance splits change and the M1-vs-M5 comparison decks are reinterpreted
The same claim underwrites how the M5-vs-data plots are read, since it asserts all four on-disk fits share one α_v
The cited line ranges (Params.jl 239–245 vs 287–293) can drift as those files change, making the 'line for line identical' claim silently false

expectation: Unknown. If the claim holds, no numerics move — the text is descriptive. If α_v is not 0.3 in all four fits, or the cascades have diverged, the stated M1/M5 equivalence and the "difference is purely topological" conclusion are wrong. I cannot tell which from the context given.

check.why: Cheaply tests the two load-bearing claims: that α_v defaults to 0.3 in both models' Params.jl, and that no fit config under Model_5/fits frees or overrides it. No solve or re-fit needed.
